question.text:
Consider the following differential equation. \[ y'' + y' - 12y = 14xe^{-4x} \] The general solution to this equation can be written as \[ y(x) = A e^{-4x} + B e^{3x} + g(x), \] where $A$ and $B$ are constants. Which of the following could be the function $g(x)?$

Hint: Use the variation of parameters method. You may also wish to make use of the following result (integration constants omitted): \[ \int x e^{-7x} \,\textrm{d}x = - \dfrac{1}{49}(7x + 1)e^{-7x} \]

question.text:
Consider the following differential equation \[ y''+4y'+5y=e^{-2x}\sec{x}. \]

The general solution to this equation can be written as \[ y(x)=e^{-2x}\bigl(A\cos x + B\sin x\bigr)+g(x), \] where $A$ and $B$ are constants. Which of the following could be the function $g(x)?$

Hint: Use the variation of parameters method. You may also wish to make use of the following result (integration constant omitted): \[ \int \tan x\,\textrm{d}x=-\ln|\cos x| \]

question.text:
Consider the following differential equation \[ y'' + 9y = 27\sin{3x}\cos{3x}. \]

The general solution to this equation can be written as \[ y(x) = A\cos{3x} + B\sin{3x} - g(x), \] where $A$ and $B$ are constants. Which of the following could be the function $g(x)?$

Hint: Use the variation of parameters method. You may also wish to make use of the following results (integration constants omitted):

\begin{align*} \int \sin^2 3x \cos 3x\,\textrm{d}x&=\dfrac19\sin^3 {3x} \\[5pt] \int \cos^2 3x \sin 3x\,\textrm{d}x&=-\dfrac19\cos^3 {3x} \end{align*}
